chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: 'Do you know why three (Sacred Monuments) have been placed there?' I said, 'No'. He said: 'So whoever attains any one of them, has attained the Hajj.'

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ: Attained/Reached (in the context of performing a ritual)
key_terms.ثَلَاثٌ: Three (referring to the three major mosques/sacred sites)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on attaining Hajj by visiting one of the three sacred sites?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal principle of *kifayah* (sufficiency) regarding the three major sanctuaries: Mecca, Medina, and Jerusalem. He establishes that for one who is unable to visit all three, performing the requisite rituals at any single one of these Sacred Monuments is legally sufficient to discharge the obligation of Hajj, reflecting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence for those with limited means or capacity.
